name: Easy Slow-Cooker Pork Ragù

ingredients.name: St. Louis–cut ribs
ingredients.prep: cut between bones into 3 equal pieces

instructions.primary_message: Cut the St. Louis–cut ribs between bones into 3 equal pieces. Finely chop the yellow onion. Finely chop the carrots. Mince the garlic.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 rack St. Louis–cut ribs
1 medium yellow onion
2 medium carrots
3 cloves garlic

instructions.primary_message: Sprinkle rib portions evenly all over with 2 teaspoons salt and pepper, rubbing seasoning into ribs so it adheres; set aside.
In the slow cooker, add onion, carrot, garlic, rosemary, thyme, bay leaf, passata, chicken stock, red wine, tomato paste, olive oil, and remaining 1 teaspoon salt. Whisk vigorously to combine well.

Nestle pork ribs into sauce, turning to coat and laying flat to cover with liquid as much as possible. Cover and cook until pork is tender and falling off the bone, 6 to 7 hours on high or 8 to 10 hours on low.

Use tongs to discard rosemary sprig, thyme, and bay leaf. If needed, use a ladle or wide spoon to skim excess fat from the top of sauce. Use tongs to remove the rib bones. The bones should slide off the meat easily. Keeping everything in the slow cooker, use a potato masher to mash until meat is broken down into small shreds and bite-sized pieces.

To serve, in a large pot, cook pasta in a pot of boiling salted water until just shy of al dente (about 1 minute for fresh pasta or 1 minute short of recommended cooking time for dried pasta). Drain, reserving about 1 cup of starchy pasta water. Return pasta to the pot you just cooked it in and add half of ragù, ½ cup cooking water; reserve remaining ragù for future use (see notes). Cook over medium-high heat, stirring until the sauce emulsifies with the pasta water and clings to the pasta, adding more pasta water a few tablespoons at a time if necessary. Serve immediately.

schema_metadata.keywords: Slow-Cooker Pork Ragù, slow-cooker recipe, pork ragu recipe, pork ragu

description: This easy slow-cooker pork ragù made with St. Louis–cut ribs delivers rich, Italian-American Sunday gravy flavor—no browning required.
notes:
Optional substitutions: homemade chicken stock → store-bought low-sodium broth

Notes: Passata di pomodoro is a cooked tomato puree that can be made at home or purchased in jars at most supermarkets.
This recipe makes about 6 cups of ragù, enough to sauce about 0.91 kg of pasta. Three cups of ragù (half of this recipe) will sauce about 0.45 kg of pasta. I like to freeze the remaining ragù for later use.

Make-ahead and storage: The ragù can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 5 days or frozen for up to 2 months.
author: Leah Colins
